questions.question: What is collaborative filtering?

options.text: A method that uses item features for recommendations.
A technique that predicts user preferences based on past behavior.
A way to filter out noise from data.
A strategy that combines multiple recommendation methods.

questions.explanation: Collaborative filtering predicts user preferences based on the behavior of similar users.

questions.question: What does content-based filtering rely on?
questions.explanation: Content-based filtering recommends items based on their features and the user's preferences.

questions.question: Hybrid recommender systems combine multiple recommendation techniques.
questions.explanation: Hybrid systems leverage both collaborative and content-based filtering to improve recommendations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a limitation of collaborative filtering?

options.text: It requires a large amount of data.
It is always more accurate than content-based filtering.
It does not consider user preferences.

questions.explanation: Collaborative filtering relies on user data, so it struggles with sparse datasets.
